nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field with algebraic closure $\bar k$, let $Z \subseteq \bar k^n$, and let $f \in I_k(Z)$. Then for every point $P \in Z$, the image of $f$ in $\bar k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ evaluated at $P$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Polynomials in the ideal over $k$ vanish on the set

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field with algebraic closure $\bar k$. If $Z_1 \subseteq Z_2 \subseteq \bar k^n$, then $I_k(Z_2) \subseteq I_k(Z_1)$.
nodes.title: The ideal over $k$ reverses inclusions

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field with algebraic closure $\bar k$. For every $n$, the ideal $I_k(\emptyset)$ of the empty subset of $\bar k^n$ is all of $k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$.
nodes.title: The ideal over $k$ of the empty set

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field with algebraic closure $\bar k$, and let $Z \subseteq \bar k^n$. The ideal $I_k(Z)$ of $k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ consists of the polynomials $f$ with coefficients in $k$ whose image in $\bar k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ vanishes at every point of $Z$; that is, $I_k(Z)$ is the preimage of the vanishing ideal of $Z$ in $\bar k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ under the coefficient map…
nodes.title: Ideal over $k$ of a subset of affine space

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field with algebraic closure $\bar k$ and let $Z \subseteq \bar k^n$. Then $Z$ is defined over $k$ if and only if the vanishing ideal of $Z$ in $\bar k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ equals the ideal generated by the image of $I_k(Z)$ under the coefficient map $k[X_1, \dots, X_n] \to \bar k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$.
nodes.title: Defined over $k$ as an equality of ideals

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field with algebraic closure $\bar k$, let $Z \subseteq \bar k^n$, and let $I_k(Z)$ be the ideal of polynomials in $k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ whose image in $\bar k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ vanishes at every point of $Z$. The set $Z$ is defined over $k$ if the vanishing ideal of $Z$ in $\bar k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ equals the ideal generated by the image of $I_k(Z)$ under the coefficient map…
nodes.title: Sets defined over $k$

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field with algebraic closure $\bar k$, let $Z \subseteq \bar k^n$, and let $f \in k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$. Then $f$ lies in the ideal $I_k(Z)$ over $k$ of $Z$ if and only if the image of $f$ in $\bar k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ under the coefficient map lies in the vanishing ideal of $Z$, that is, vanishes at every point of $Z$.
nodes.title: Membership in the ideal over $k$
